summary: Wat Mahathat Yuwaratrangsarit’s International Vipassana Meditation Centre offers English-language meditation instruction in the Rattanakosin historic district. It is a practical short practice session rather than a guaranteed December retreat: verify the exact class and language before travelling.
whyGo: Try guided Vipassana meditation in English at an active Bangkok temple, away from the pace of the main sightseeing circuit.
Pair a morning or afternoon session with Tha Phra Chan, the Grand Palace area or the riverfront.
bestFor: Visitors curious about Buddhist meditation who can follow temple etiquette and sit quietly for an extended session.
Travellers wanting a structured cultural experience in the historic centre.
skipIf: You need a confirmed December 2026 class time, guaranteed English guidance or an accessible step-free route without checking directly first.
You want a multi-day residential retreat; the available current listings describe day sessions.
duration: Allow about 2.5 hours for a session, based on the centre listing’s current 08:00–10:30 and 13:00–15:30 sessions, plus travel time. December dates and times are not yet confirmed.
cost: The Tourism Authority of Thailand lists temple admission as free. No current meditation-class fee is published in the sources checked; ask the centre whether a voluntary donation is customary.
hours: TAT lists the temple as open daily 07:30–18:00. This is the temple’s general visiting window, not confirmation that the meditation centre or a class is open at all those times.
bestTime: Choose a scheduled morning session if available, then continue sightseeing before the midday heat. Check the session date and language shortly before your visit.
gettingThere: The temple is at 3 Tha Phra Chan Road in Phra Nakhon, near Thammasat University. Tha Chang is the nearest Chao Phraya Express Boat pier according to Travelfish; from there, walk toward the Grand Palace/Tha Phra Chan area and ask for the International Vipassana Meditation Centre, Section 5. Allow extra time in the historic district and confirm the exact entrance locally.
booking: A current listing shows scheduled English day sessions, but no December 2026 timetable is available yet. Contact the meditation centre before setting out to confirm the date, language, entry procedure and whether advance registration is needed. TAT lists the meditation-centre phone as +66 2 222 6011; verify the number still works before relying on it.
accessibility: Accessibility information for the meditation centre was not found. Ask about steps, seating, toilets and accommodation for mobility or sensory needs before visiting; the temple complex is historic and routes may include uneven surfaces.
practicalTips: Dress modestly: cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes where instructed, and follow staff directions in practice areas.
Arrive early enough to locate Section 5 and check in; bring water and wear comfortable clothing suitable for sitting quietly.
Treat the session as religious practice: keep phones silent and ask before taking photographs.
decemberNotes: December is a popular Bangkok travel period. The temple’s general hours are listed year-round, but no specific December 2026 meditation dates or holiday adjustments were published in the sources checked. Reconfirm the class close to your visit, especially around public holidays and year-end.
uncertainties: The English class schedule, registration policy and any donation expectation for December 2026 are not confirmed.
The current schedule listing is third-party; the center’s own page found during research did not provide a usable timetable or practical visitor details.
Accessibility and suitability for visitors with specific support needs are not documented in the sources checked.
